sentences.text: On the FIR lodged by the petitioner, respondent nos.2 to 5 have been charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 r/w 34 of IPC alleging that they subjected the petitioner to cruelty both mentally and physically.

The petitioner has annexed a copy of the memorandum of agreement dated 31.08.2023 under Section 89 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with Rules 24 and 25 of the Karnataka Civil Procedure (Mediation) Rules, 2005.

A perusal of the memorandum of agreement indicated that the petitioner had filed a petition in M.C.No.279/2023 for dissolving her marriage with respondent no.2 under Section 10(i)(viii) of the Divorce Act.

The matter was referred to the Mediation Centre,
Mangaluru, to explore the possibility of settlement between the parties.

3. Before the Mediation Centre, the parties have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves,
and in terms of the settlement, their marriage has been dissolved mutually, and the petitioner has agreed that she would withdraw the impugned proceedings.

4. Though the offences alleged are cognizable and non-compoundable, however, having regard to the fact NC: 2023:KHC:41018 that the parties have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves, it would be a futile exercise, if respondent nos.2 to 5 are subjected to trial, since the probability of their conviction is remote and bleak in view of the settlement.
Therefore, the continuation of criminal proceedings against them will be an abuse of the process of law.
5. Accordingly, the criminal petition is allowed.
The impugned proceedings in CC No.1779/2020 on the file of JMFC III Court, Dakshina Kannada, Mangaluru stands quashed.
